end.summary:
- Practised making one mark for each object.
- Practised matching marks to objects to find missing or extra items.
- Explained a boat-and-stone tracking method with support.
- Initially said a spread-out row had more objects; later corrected this and said the rows were equal.
- Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Parth practised keeping track by pairing each object with one mark, using stones as an example. They described placing one stone for each boat and removing one when a boat returned. They repeatedly mixed up spread-out objects with having more, but later corrected this by saying two and two were equal and that spreading only made the bangles seem like more. At home, place two groups of buttons in different spacing and ask Parth to match them one-to-one without counting.
